title: Models Are Getting Dumber on Purpose: The Trade-Off Between Reasoning and Factual Knowledge in AI
summary: The article explores the deliberate shift in AI model development toward prioritizing reasoning capabilities over factual knowledge retention. Modern models like GLM-5.2, Qwen3.5, and DeepSeek V4-Flash demonstrate significant improvements in math and coding benchmarks while reducing active parameter counts. However, this comes at the cost of factual recall, with even top models like Gemini 2.5 Pro scoring only 53% on factual benchmarks like SimpleQA. The trade-off is intentional: reasoning compresses efficiently, while facts require substantial parameter space and degrade over time. This approach decouples static model weights from dynamic real-world knowledge, relying instead on external 'harnesses' (e.g., retrieval systems, tool calls) to supply up-to-date information. The result is smaller, more efficient models that can run on consumer GPUs but require robust external knowledge sources to mitigate hallucinations and outdated information.
key_points: Modern AI models are prioritizing reasoning over factual knowledge, leading to smaller, more efficient architectures with fewer active parameters per token.
Benchmarks show dramatic improvements in math and coding tasks (e.g., GLM-5.2 scores 99.2% on AIME 2026), but factual recall remains poor (e.g., Gemini 2.5 Pro scores 53% on SimpleQA).
Facts require significant parameter space (estimated at ~2 bits per parameter) and degrade over time, while reasoning procedures compress efficiently and remain stable.
The shift is deliberate: models are designed to be generalists with broad but shallow knowledge, relying on external systems (harnesses) for depth and up-to-date information.
This approach decouples expensive, slow model training from rapidly changing factual knowledge, reducing the need for frequent retraining.
Smaller models (20-40B parameters) can run on consumer GPUs (e.g., 24GB VRAM) but require robust retrieval systems or tool calls to compensate for limited factual knowledge.
Hallucinations are mitigated when facts are stored externally, as wrong answers can be traced to source documents and corrected without retraining the model.
Future models may eliminate knowledge cutoffs entirely, relying entirely on runtime-supplied information, similar to how a CPU loads a program.
